rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (score 158.144, up from 53.26): the oval now finishes 5 of 20 trials (mean finish 1.87 s, progress 0.55), so ki=0.4 and the wider sensors helped there. The s-bend and slalom still go off track in all 40 trials. Progress is only 0.11 to 0.17, so the robot leaves the line early on the tighter bends. Each run logs about one line-loss event, max_error sits at about 0.061 to 0.062 m against the 0.06 m limit, and steering oscillation is low (0.15 to 0.22). The failure is therefore an early overshoot or drift into a bend at speed, not jitter. The evaluator's conditional rule applies: progress is well below 0.5 on the failing tracks. Change: lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.2 and keep every other value fixed, so the effect of speed is isolated. The scaling from oval finish times suggests about 2.5 s at 1.2 (1.87 s × 1.6/1.2), which stays under the 3.0 s limit. Expected result: fewer off-track exits on s-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.05 m, progress above 0.5 on those tracks, and more oval finishes. Hypotheses: (H1) speed is the main cause of early departure on bends; (H2) if speed alone does not fix s-bend and slalom, the outer sensors (x=±0.04) are losing the line on the sharp bends, and widening them (x=±0.06) is the next step. Measurements to check next: completion_time on the oval (should stay under 3.0 s), progress and max_error on s-bend and slalom, and line_loss_events per track.
